analysis:
This batch contains documentation only. One file was added: changelog.d/gptoss-bf16-activations.md (head lines 1-22). One line was changed: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md line 113 on both base and head.

The changelog says the GPT-OSS SwiGLU clamp bounds now take the activation dtype. As a result, bf16 activations and K/V are kept on every layer. The per-token K/V bytes are halved, and the heartbeat kv_bytes_per_token halves accordingly. Output is no longer bit-identical to the float32 path; top-1 agreement with float32 is 93.3%. SSD complete checkpoints written with float32 layer types fall into a different checkpoint namespace and are not restored. The 3.5 GiB activation floor is unchanged and was not re-measured with bf16 activations.

No implementation source is in this batch, so none of these claims were verified against code. Relevant threat entries:
- T-041 (SSD prefix cache): the claimed namespace separation by layer dtype is fail-closed, since it adds cold prefill only. It changes no HMAC naming, TTL, AAD or scope salt.
- T-007/T-027 (output integrity): the numeric drift is a model-quality change, not an integrity bypass. The coordinator's weight/build identity is unaffected.
- Availability (memory admission): an activation floor measured on float32 should be conservative if bf16 activations are smaller. The docs also note it was not re-measured.
- Heartbeat capacity: the halved kv_bytes_per_token is a platform contract question. Check it against the platform memorypolicy referenced at hardware-support.md line 459.

Integration should verify the following in the actual Swift/MLX changes, if they are in other batches:
- The clamp dtype change.
- Checkpoint identity including the per-layer dtype, so float32 checkpoints are never imported into bf16 slots.
- Admission using the observed native K/V dtype.

No security regression was identified in these documentation units.
